regions.name: Europe
regions.blurb: Most of Europe is covered by the Schengen Area: one short-stay visa policy for 29 countries, with ETIAS pre-travel authorisation being phased in for visa-exempt visitors and the EES biometric entry system now operating at external borders.

regions.name: Southeast Asia
regions.blurb: Visa policy varies widely across Southeast Asia — from broad visa exemptions in Thailand and Malaysia to eVisa regimes in Vietnam, Indonesia and Cambodia. Digital arrival cards are increasingly mandatory across the region.

regions.name: East Asia
regions.blurb: Japan, South Korea and Taiwan offer generous visa waivers to many passports, while mainland China combines visa exemptions with a large embassy-visa system. Electronic arrival procedures are standard.

regions.name: South Asia
regions.blurb: India, Sri Lanka and Nepal run large eVisa or on-arrival programmes; requirements vary sharply by nationality, and yellow fever certificates are checked for travellers arriving from risk countries.

regions.name: Middle East
regions.blurb: The Gulf states run modern eVisa and on-arrival systems; Saudi Arabia requires specific vaccinations for Hajj and Umrah pilgrims. Israel entry stamps can affect onward travel in parts of the region.

regions.name: Africa
regions.blurb: Many African countries have moved to eVisa portals. Yellow fever vaccination certificates (ICVP) are a common entry condition, either universally or when arriving from a risk country.

regions.name: Americas
regions.blurb: The United States (ESTA) and Canada (eTA) require electronic travel authorisation from visa-waiver nationals; most of Latin America is visa-free for Western passports, with proof of onward travel commonly checked.

regions.name: Oceania
regions.blurb: Australia (ETA/eVisitor) and New Zealand (NZeTA) require electronic authorisation from nearly all visitors; Pacific island states are largely visa-free or visa-on-arrival.
